question.leadin: A period of expansion into Germany under this ruler was ended by defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
question.text: Name this first Emperor of Rome, who conquered Egypt through victory at the Battle of Actium.
question.answerHtml: Octavian [or Augustus Caesar or Gaius Octavius; do not accept or prompt on just “Caesar”]
question.clue: The Second Triumvirate consisted of Antony, Lepidus, and this adopted son of Julius Caesar, who fought a civil war against Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE and became the first Emperor of Rome.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman Britain.
swap.text: This structure marked the northern boundary of Roman Britain. It stretches across northern England and is named for the emperor who built it.
swap.clue: A birthday invitation was found on one of the Vindolanda tablets, which were unearthed near this structure.

question.leadin: Bridges are often important military objectives, as they can create chokepoints to slow an army's advance or retreat.
question.text: In 312 CE, Constantine I soundly defeated Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge, which spans this major river of Rome. Maxentius drowned in this river's waters during the battle.
question.clue: The first colonia was a city at the mouth of this river which imported grain and was named Ostia.

swap.leadin: The eventual losing side in this conflict was expelled from the Iberian Peninsula with their loss at the Battle of Ilipa.
swap.text: Identify this conflict whose notable leaders included Mago and Hasdrubal, the latter of whom led troops in losing efforts at the Battles of Baecula and the Metaurus.
swap.clue: The deadliest battle in this war saw Paullus and Varro drawn into a double encirclement and lose 50 000 men.

question.text: The First and Second Servile Wars were fought in Sicily, but the Third Servile War ended when this Thracian man was killed in battle and six thousand former slaves were crucified along the Appian Way.
question.clue: This Thracian lends his name to a league co-founded by Rosa Luxemburg in 20th-century Germany.

swap.leadin: While accounting the results of this battle to his country's senate, Mago poured out dozens of golden rings captured from the enemy.
swap.text: Name this greatest Roman defeat during the Republic Era, in which Hannibal Barca used his pincer strategy. This battle resulted in the adoption of the Fabian strategy by Rome.
swap.clue: Eight legions - the most then assembled - took part in this clash, an obsession of von Schlieffen, which led to the principes being deployed farther behind the hastati and the permanent adoption of the strategy of Fabius Cunctator.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about historical events that appear in the worksof the Roman historian Tacitus.
question.text: According to Tacitus, this ruler of the Iceni revolted against Roman rule after the death of Prasutagus. Suetonius Paulinus ultimately defeated this ruler near Paulerspury.
question.clue: This leader's first target was Camulondunum, which was burned to the ground after the defeat of the Ninth Legion.

swap.leadin: Caracalla is presented by many sources as a tyrant, but he wasn't all bad.
swap.text: One of Caracalla's great public projects was the construction of his namesake one of the these things, the second-largest in Rome. These places were fed water by aqueducts which was then heated by log fires.
swap.clue: Slaves called unctores would often use a strigil on their masters in the destrictarium of these places.

question.leadin: Identify these regions subject to military incursions by Roman forces.
question.text: Decebalus's raids from this region prompted Domitian to launch the first of two namesake wars, whose second incarnation saw Trajan subjugate this region bounded by the Danube and the Carpathians. Its capital was at Sarmizegetusa.
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.text: Tarquinius Superbus fled to this king of Clusium, whose campaign to reinstall the king was foiled by the determination of Mucius Scaevola.
swap.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

question.leadin: This king legendarily purchased the three Syllibine Books after six of the original nine were burned in a negotiation ploy.
question.text: Name this last king of Rome. This despot of Etruscan descent was overthrown after his son raped Lucretia.
question.answerHtml: Tarquin the Proud [or Tarquinius Superbus; do not accept “Tarquinius Priscus”]
question.clue: Lars Porcena was ostensibly helping this man regain his control of Rome. This man, supposedly the son of an earlier king with a similar name, lost power after his son raped Lucretia.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the lives of women in the Roman world.
swap.text: One important religious position held exclusively by women was this group of female priests. They were held to be incorruptible, and tended to the sacred fire of the goddess of the hearth.
swap.clue: Livy claimed that a traitorous member of this group was crushed by the shields of the Sabines and then thrown from the namesake Tarpeian Rock.

question.text: Before fleeing to the Balearics, Mago was defeated at this battle near Seville by a concealed force of Romans under Scipio Africanus. The battle of Baecula and this battle ended Carthaginian power in Spain.
question.clue: This battle's victor unusually placed legions on the wings and auxiliaries in the centre, later creating a concave formation that mirrored a battle occurring ten years prior.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about religion in ancient Rome.
swap.text: Not to be confused with Saturnalia, this festival took place in mid-February and featured the sacrifice of a goat and a dog, after which the priests would run through town and slap people with the skin of the goat.
swap.clue: This event originated when King Amulius ordered two men to be thrown into the Tiber River as punishment.

question.leadin: Tarquin the Proud refused to buy these documents at first, leading 6 of them to be burnt.
question.text: Name these documents written in hexameter that were stored in the Temple of Jupiter Capitolinus and guarded by the Decemviri Sacris Faciundis. The general Flavius Stilicho supposedly ordered that they be destroyed.

swap.text: This very first pope is the patron saint of bakers and Las Vegas. He's often depicted standing at the gates of heaven allowing people in.
swap.clue: Piux IX installed a statue of this first pope in his namesake basilica in the Vatican. As an apostle this man denied Jesus three times.

question.text: This confederate of the lawyer Celestius wrote the tract On Free Will but was condemned by Pope Zosimus at the Council of Carthage for his belief in the ability of men to save themselves.
question.clue: This British heretic, who famously denied original sin and incurred the wrath of St. Augustine.

swap.leadin: Appius Claudius precipitated the first of these events by passing a law that reinforced the right of creditors to imprison their debtors.
swap.text: Identify these events, of which there were at least five in total. The second of them was a protest against the abuses of the decemviri, or the men who implemented the Twelve Tables.
swap.answerHtml: plebeian secessions [or secessions of the plebs; or secessio plebis; accept synonyms for “secession” such as withdrawal; prompt on “secession” or “withdrawal”]

question.text: Curzio Inghirami botched his staged discoveries of Etruscan "scariths" by using paper instead of this material. The Zagreb Book is an Etruscan text written on this material that was found wrapped around an Egyptian mummy.
question.answerHtml: linen [or flax; accept Liber Linteus, Libri lintei, or linen rolls; prompt on textiles, fabric, or synonyms]

swap.leadin: Since this woman accompanied her husband on his military campaigns, she may have been mentioned in the lost epic about him by Gaius Albinovanus Pedo.
swap.text: Name this granddaughter of Augustus who was married to her second cousin Germanicus to place him in the line of succession for the Roman throne.
swap.answerHtml: Agrippina the Elder [or Agrippina Major; or Agrippina Germanici; prompt on Agrippina]
